stem: Unless a different limit is posted, what is the speed limit in an Ohio school zone during school hours?
explanation:
Ohio law sets **20 mph** in **school zones** during school recess and while children are going to or leaving school at opening and closing hours, where school speed limit signs are posted.

**Wrong choices**
- 15 mph: 15 mph is the limit for alleys within a city or village.
- 25 mph: 25 mph is the usual limit in other parts of a city or village.
- 35 mph: 35 mph is the limit on state routes in a city or village outside business districts.

stem: Unless a different limit is posted, what is the speed limit on a residential street in an Ohio city or village?
explanation:
Ohio law sets **25 mph** for most parts of a city or village (a municipal corporation), including **residential streets**, unless a different limit is posted.

**Wrong choices**
- 20 mph: 20 mph is the school zone limit during school hours.
- 35 mph: 35 mph is for state routes in a city or village outside business districts.
- 45 mph: 45 mph is not a default limit for residential streets.

stem: How close to a fire hydrant may you park?
oneLineConcept: Fire hydrant: no parking within 10 feet
explanation:
Ohio law says you may not park **within 10 feet of a fire hydrant**. Firefighters need room to reach and connect to it.

**Wrong choices**
- No closer than 5 feet: 5 feet is closer than the law allows.
- No closer than 20 feet: 20 feet is the distance from a crosswalk at an intersection.
- No closer than 30 feet: 30 feet is the distance from a stop sign, yield sign, or traffic signal.

stem: Another driver is passing you on a two-lane road. What should you do?
choices: Move toward the center line to block the pass
Speed up so the other driver cannot cut in
Keep right and do not speed up until the other car has passed
oneLineConcept: Being passed: keep right, do not speed up
explanation:
Ohio law says the driver being passed must **give way to the right** and **must not increase speed** until the other vehicle has completely passed.

**Wrong choices**
- Move toward the center line to block the pass: Blocking a passing driver can cause a head-on crash.
- Speed up so the other driver cannot cut in: Speeding up while being passed is against the law and dangerous.
- Brake hard right away: Braking hard can cause a crash from behind. Simply keep your speed and stay right.

stem: You are passing a car on a two-lane road. Before you come within what distance of an oncoming vehicle must you be back in your own lane?
oneLineConcept: Passing: be back before you are within 200 feet of oncoming traffic
explanation:
When passing uses the lane for oncoming traffic, Ohio law says you must return to your lane **before coming within 200 feet** of any oncoming vehicle. If you cannot do that safely, do not start the pass.

**Wrong choices**
- 50 feet: 50 feet is far too close to an oncoming vehicle.
- 100 feet: 100 feet is the no-passing distance near intersections and railroad crossings, not this rule.
- 500 feet: 500 feet is not the number in this rule.

stem: Unless a different limit is posted, what is the speed limit on most highways outside cities and villages in Ohio?
explanation:
Ohio law sets **55 mph** on highways **outside municipal corporations** (cities and villages), unless another limit applies or is posted. Some roads have higher limits, such as **70 mph on rural freeways**.

**Wrong choices**
- 45 mph: 45 mph is not the default limit for these highways.
- 65 mph: 65 mph applies to certain expressways and urban freeways, not most highways.
- 70 mph: 70 mph is for rural freeways only.

stem: How close to a crosswalk at an intersection may you park?
oneLineConcept: Crosswalk at an intersection: no parking within 20 feet
explanation:
Ohio law says you may not park **within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection**. Parked cars there would hide people who are about to cross.

**Wrong choices**
- No closer than 10 feet: 10 feet is the distance from a fire hydrant.
- No closer than 30 feet: 30 feet is the distance from a stop sign, yield sign, or traffic signal.
- No closer than 50 feet: 50 feet is the distance from the nearest rail of a railroad crossing.

stem: How close to a stop sign, yield sign, or traffic signal may you park on the approach to it?
oneLineConcept: Stop sign, yield sign, or signal: no parking within 30 feet
explanation:
Ohio law says you may not park **within 30 feet** of, and on the approach to, a **stop sign, yield sign, or traffic signal**. Parked cars there would block drivers' view of the sign or signal.

**Wrong choices**
- No closer than 10 feet: 10 feet is the distance from a fire hydrant.
- No closer than 20 feet: 20 feet is the distance from a crosswalk at an intersection.
- No closer than 50 feet: 50 feet is the distance from the nearest rail of a railroad crossing.

stem: How close to the nearest rail of a railroad crossing may you park?
oneLineConcept: Railroad crossing: no parking within 50 feet of the nearest rail
explanation:
Ohio law says you may not park **within 50 feet of the nearest rail** of a railroad crossing.

**Wrong choices**
- No closer than 15 feet: 15 feet is the closest you may stop when a train is coming, not a parking distance.
- No closer than 30 feet: 30 feet is the distance from a stop sign, yield sign, or traffic signal.
- No closer than 100 feet: 100 feet is the no-passing distance near a railroad crossing, not the parking rule.

stem: Ohio's assured clear distance ahead rule means you must drive at a speed that lets you do what?
choices: Keep up with the flow of traffic at all times
Stop within the distance you can clearly see ahead
Stay exactly 2 car lengths behind the car ahead
Reach the speed limit within a short distance
oneLineConcept: Assured clear distance: be able to stop within what you can see
explanation:
Ohio law says no one may drive faster than will let them **bring the vehicle to a stop within the assured clear distance ahead**. At night, in fog, or on a curve you can see less, so you must slow down.

**Wrong choices**
- Keep up with the flow of traffic at all times: Keeping up with traffic is not a defense if you cannot stop in time.
- Stay exactly 2 car lengths behind the car ahead: The rule is about seeing and stopping, not a set number of car lengths.
- Reach the speed limit within a short distance: The rule limits your speed. It is not about reaching the limit.

stem: On a two-lane road, when may you NOT drive on the left side to pass?
choices: When you are more than 500 feet from an intersection
When you are within 100 feet of an intersection or railroad crossing
When the center line is broken on your side
When the vehicle ahead is going under the speed limit
oneLineConcept: No left-side driving within 100 ft of an intersection or rail crossing
explanation:
Ohio law says you may not drive on the left side of the road when you are **within 100 feet of, or crossing, an intersection or railroad crossing**. The same applies near the top of a hill or on a curve where you cannot see, and within 100 feet of a bridge, viaduct, or tunnel when your view is blocked.

**Wrong choices**
- When you are more than 500 feet from an intersection: Being far from an intersection does not by itself make passing unlawful.
- When the center line is broken on your side: A broken line on your side allows passing when it is safe.
- When the vehicle ahead is going under the speed limit: Passing a slower vehicle is allowed when it is otherwise safe and legal.

stem: When does Ohio law allow you to pass another vehicle on the right?
choices: Any time the vehicle ahead is going below the speed limit
When the vehicle ahead is turning left, or the road has room for two or more lanes going your way
Only on a road with one lane in each direction
When you can use the paved shoulder
oneLineConcept: Passing on the right: only when legal and on the roadway
explanation:
You may pass on the right only when the vehicle ahead is **making or about to make a left turn**, or on a road with **enough room for two or more lanes** of traffic moving your way. You must **never drive off the roadway**, such as onto the shoulder, to pass.

**Wrong choices**
- Any time the vehicle ahead is going below the speed limit: Slower speed alone does not make passing on the right legal.
- Only on a road with one lane in each direction: A one-lane road in your direction usually leaves no room to pass on the right unless the vehicle ahead is turning left.
- When you can use the paved shoulder: Ohio law forbids passing by driving off the roadway.
